payload.description_html: Changzhousaurus is a paravian theropod dinosaur, though more specific affinities are unclear, showing derived traits of both troodontidae and dromaeosauridae. It was very small, reaching about a third of a meter in body length. Fossil remains preserve a tail-fan similar to a peacock's, and long pennaceous feathers forming wings on the forelimbs and legs.
